newsitem.title: USA: You can say that again, Mr. Dole.
newsitem.headline: You can say that again, Mr. Dole.

text.p: Face it, there is only so much new a presidential candidate can say after a lifetime in politics and a year of campaigning.
So Bob Dole just says it again, and again, and again.

As he slogs through a 96-hour "non-stop" campaign marathon leading up to Tuesday's election, the Republican presidential candidate's stump speech is more or less the same in each venue, as it has been for most of the campaign.
But Dole delivers it like a jazz performance -- a one-man improvised jam of freely associated riffs on familiar themes, shaped by the mood of the crowd and of the candidate.
A major hallmark of his style, clearly refined by the grueling campaign push, is repetition, as these selections from the marathon illustrate:
-- "Do you want the truth for a change? You can do it on Tuesday. The truth for a change! The truth for a change! The truth for a change!"
-- "We are going to give America back to the people! Back to the people! Back to the people!"
-- "And I would say to all the soccer moms out there, we're gonna sock it to 'em when it comes to the drug dealers. We're gonna sock it to 'em! Sock it to 'em! Sock it to 'em!"
-- "He (Clinton) says 'I've created 11 million jobs.' Yeah, I met a guy the other day who's got three of 'em. You got to have three just to pay the bills! To pay the bills! To pay the bills!"
-- "Phase two (of a planned tax overhaul) is a flatter, fairer, simpler tax. And end the IRS as we know it! End the IRS as we know it! End the IRS as we know it!"
-- "Public trust! Public trust! Public trust! Do not violate the public trust!"
-- "We're going to keep on campaigning non-stop until I vote in Russell Kansas at noon on Tuesday .... Ninety-six hours. Non-stop! Non-stop! Non-stop! Non-stop! Non-stop!"
Now what does he do for an encore?
